testName: IISER IAT Mock Test: Moving Charges and Magnetism (Version 2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charged particle moves freely through a region of space containing a uniform, steady magnetic field. In the absence of any other forces, which of the particle's physical properties must remain strictly constant throughout its motion?
questions.explanation: The magnetic Lorentz force F = q(v × B) is strictly perpendicular to velocity. Because the force is perpendicular to displacement, work done W = 0. By the Work-Energy Theorem, kinetic energy remains perfectly constant. Velocity and momentum change direction continually.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two long, straight, perfectly parallel wires are placed parallel to each other in a vacuum. If they carry steady electrical currents in *opposite* directions, the magnetic force between them is:
options: Directed perpendicular to the plane containing the wires
questions.explanation: When two parallel wires carry currents in anti-parallel directions, the magnetic field generated by the first wire forces the charges in the second wire away. Thus, by the Lorentz force and right-hand rule, anti-parallel currents strictly repel each other.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the equivalent magnetic dipole moment (M) of a closely wound, flat circular coil having N turns, cross-sectional area A, and carrying a steady current I?
questions.explanation: A planar current loop acts natively as a magnetic dipole. The magnitude of the magnetic dipole moment is the product of turns N, current I, and area A. Thus, M = N I A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A moving coil galvanometer can be successfully converted into a voltmeter capable of measuring large potential differences. This conversion requires connecting:
options: A low resistance in series with the galvanometer.
A high resistance in series with the galvanometer.
A low resistance in parallel with the galvanometer.
A high resistance in parallel with the galvanometer.
questions.explanation: A voltmeter connects in parallel and must draw minimal current. To restrict the current flowing through the sensitive galvanometer and measure high voltages, a very high resistance must be placed strictly in series with it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An ideal solenoid of total length L and total turns N carries a steady current I. The magnitude of the magnetic field precisely at one of its open ends is approximately:
questions.explanation: The magnetic field deep inside an ideal solenoid is B = μ₀ n I = (μ₀ N I)/L. Due to symmetry and field lines diverging at the edges, the field exactly at an open end is precisely half of the internal field. Thus, B_end = (μ₀ N I) / 2L.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The international standard unit of current (1 Ampere) is defined as the constant current which, if maintained in two straight parallel conductors of infinite length placed 1 meter apart in a vacuum, produces a mutual force per unit length equal to:
questions.explanation: The SI definition of the Ampere relies on f = (μ₀ I₁ I₂) / (2π d). Given I₁ = I₂ = 1 A, d = 1 m, and μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A, the force is f = (4π × 10⁻⁷) / (2π) = 2 × 10⁻⁷ N/m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
PASSAGE: A narrow beam consists of singly ionized atoms of two distinct isotopes of an element. Their masses are m₁ and m₂ (where m₁ > m₂). The ions first pass through a velocity/energy selector and then enter a region of uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to their velocities. They trace semi-circular paths and strike a photographic plate at distances d₁ and d₂ from the entry slit.

If the ions entered the magnetic field with the exact same constant *kinetic energy* K, what is the ratio of their radii of curvature R₁ / R₂?
questions.explanation: Radius R = mv / qB. Momentum p = mv = √(2mK). Thus, R = √(2mK) / qB. For identical charge and kinetic energy, R ∝ √m. Therefore, R₁ / R₂ = √(m₁ / m₂).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: PASSAGE CONTINUED: If instead, the ions entered the magnetic field with the exact same constant *momentum* p, what would be the ratio of their radii of curvature R₁ / R₂?
questions.explanation: Radius R = p / qB. If momentum p and charge q are identical, and they enter the same B-field, every variable in the equation is identical. Thus, R₁ strictly equals R₂. The ratio is 1:1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: PASSAGE CONTINUED: If the ions were accelerated from rest through the same accelerating potential difference V before entering the magnetic field, what is the geometric separation distance (d₁ - d₂) between their striking points on the photographic plate?
questions.explanation: Accelerated via potential V, kinetic energy K = qV. Radius R = √(2m(qV)) / qB = √(2mV) / (B√q). The striking distance is the diameter d = 2R = [2√(2mV)] / (B√q). The separation is d₁ - d₂ = [2√(2V) / (B√q)] * (√m₁ - √m₂).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A long, straight hollow cylindrical pipe has an inner radius a and an outer radius b. It carries a steady current I uniformly distributed across its solid cross-section. By Ampere's Circuital Law, what is the magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance r from the central axis (where a < r < b)?
questions.explanation: Ampere's Law: B(2πr) = μ₀ I_enc. Current is uniform over area (πb² - πa²). For radius r, the enclosed area is (πr² - πa²). I_enc = I * (r² - a²)/(b² - a²). Substituting gives B =[μ₀ I (r² - a²)] / [2π r (b² - a²)].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic field due to a current element, Biot-Savart law
questions.question: A rigid wire is bent into a perfect square loop of side length a. A steady direct current I flows through the square loop. What is the exact magnitude of the magnetic field generated precisely at the geometric center of this square loop?
questions.explanation: Field from one side of the square at center (dist d=a/2, angles 45°): B₁ = (μ₀ I / 4π(a/2)) * (sin 45° + sin 45°) = (μ₀ I / 2πa) * (2/√2) = √2 μ₀ I / (2πa). Total field from 4 sides is 4 * B₁ = 4 *[√2 μ₀ I / (2πa)] = 2√2 μ₀ I / (π a).
questions.imagePrompt: A clear geometric diagram of a square loop. The side length is labeled 'a'. A circulating arrow indicates current 'I' flowing around the square. The exact geometric center is marked with a dot, indicating the point where the magnetic field is to be calculated.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A standard moving coil galvanometer has a coil resistance of 50 Ω and produces a full-scale deflection for a current of 2 mA. In order to repurpose it as a voltmeter reading up to a maximum of 10 V, what is the exact value of the resistance that must be connected in series?
questions.explanation: To convert to a voltmeter: V = I_g (R_g + R_s). 10 = 0.002 * (50 + R_s). Dividing by 0.002 gives 5000 = 50 + R_s. Solving for R_s yields 5000 - 50 = 4950 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A positively charged particle is projected along the positive x-axis (+î) into a region containing a uniform magnetic field. Upon entering, the particle immediately experiences a magnetic Lorentz force directed strictly along the positive y-axis (+ĵ). If the magnetic field is oriented strictly along one of the coordinate axes, what is its direction?
questions.explanation: Lorentz force F = q(v × B). Force is +ĵ, velocity is +î. q is positive. So, î × B must equal ĵ. Using vector cross products, we know î × (-k̂) = +ĵ. Therefore, the magnetic field must strictly point in the -k̂ direction (Negative z-direction).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic field on the axis of a circular current loop
questions.question: Two identical circular wire coils, Coil 1 and Coil 2, each of radius R, are arranged such that they share a common geometric center but their planes are perfectly mutually perpendicular. Coil 1 lies in the xy-plane and Coil 2 lies in the yz-plane. If both coils carry the same steady current I, what is the magnitude of the net magnetic field at their common center?
questions.explanation: Coil 1 (xy-plane) generates B₁ = (μ₀ I / 2R) k̂. Coil 2 (yz-plane) generates B₂ = (μ₀ I / 2R) î. These two vectors are perfectly perpendicular. The net magnetic field is the vector sum magnitude: B_net = √(|B₁|² + |B₂|²) = (μ₀ I / 2R) * √2 = √2 μ₀ I / 2R.
questions.imagePrompt: A 3D illustration showing two circular wire loops, both of identical radius R. They share exactly the same center point, but their planes are at exactly 90 degrees to each other (one horizontal, one vertical). Both carry a current labeled 'I'.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A flexible, closed circular loop of wire carries a steady clockwise current I. It is placed in a region of uniform magnetic field B. The magnetic field lines are perpendicular to the plane of the loop and point completely OUT of the page (towards the viewer). Under the influence of the magnetic force, what will physically happen to the flexible loop?
options: It will rotate about its diameter.
It will translate linearly out of the page.
questions.explanation: Magnetic force on a segment is dF = I(dl × B). For a clockwise current, look at the top segment: dl points Right. B points Out. Right × Out = Down (inward towards center). For the right segment: dl points Down. Down × Out = Left (inward). Every segment experiences a force directed radially inward. Thus, the loop will contract.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A stiff wire carrying a steady current I is physically bent to form a semi-circle of radius R. This entire semi-circular arrangement is placed in a uniform magnetic field B that acts perpendicular to the plane of the semi-circle. What is the net magnitude of the magnetic force acting on this semi-circular wire?
questions.explanation: For any uniform magnetic field, the net magnetic force on a curved wire is identical to the force on a straight wire connecting its start and end points (F = I(L_vector × B)). For a semi-circle, the straight-line displacement vector L connects the ends, making L = 2R. Since L is perpendicular to B, F = I(2R)B = 2 I B R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An electron and a proton are independently projected with the exact same initial velocity v perpendicularly into the same uniform magnetic field B. Which of the following statements rigorously describes their resulting trajectories?
options: Both particles trace identical circles but in opposite directions.
The electron traces a smaller circle and completes a revolution with a lower frequency than the proton.
The electron traces a smaller circle and completes a revolution with a much higher frequency than the proton.
The electron traces a larger circle because of its lower mass.
questions.explanation: Radius r = mv/qB. Since m_e ≪ m_p and they have the same v, q, B, the electron traces a drastically smaller circle (r_e ≪ r_p). Cyclotron frequency f = qB/(2πm). Because m is in the denominator, the much lighter electron orbits at a much higher frequency.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Three infinitely long, straight, parallel wires A, B, and C are fixed in a plane. Wire B is situated exactly midway between wires A and C. The distance between A and B is d. Wires A and C carry a steady current I in the positive y-direction. Wire B carries a steady current 2I in the negative y-direction. What is the magnitude and direction of the net magnetic force per unit length acting strictly on wire C?
options: 3μ₀ I² / (4π d), repulsive (directed away from B)
μ₀ I² / (2π d), repulsive (directed away from B)
questions.explanation: Wire C sits at x = 2d. Wire A (at 0) has current I (up). Wire C has current I (up). Parallel attracts: Force on C from A is towards A (-x), Magnitude = μ₀I² / 2π(2d) = μ₀I² / 4πd. Wire B (at d) has current 2I (down). Anti-parallel repels: Force on C from B is away from B (+x), Magnitude = μ₀(2I)(I) / 2πd = μ₀I² / πd. Net Force = (μ₀I² / πd) - (μ₀I² / 4πd) = 3μ₀I² / 4πd. Since the repulsive force from B is stronger, the net force is repulsive (away from B).
questions.imagePrompt: Three straight parallel vertical wires labeled A, B, and C from left to right. Arrows on A and C point upwards, labeled 'I'. The arrow on middle wire B points downwards, labeled '2I'. Distance markers indicate the gap between A and B is 'd', and the gap between B and C is also 'd'.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic field on the axis of a circular current loop
questions.question: A flat, non-conducting disk of radius R possesses a uniform surface charge density σ. The disk is mechanically rotated at a constant angular velocity ω about its central geometric axis. What is the exact magnitude of the magnetic field generated perfectly at the center of the disk?
questions.explanation: Consider a thin rotating ring element of radius r and width dr. Charge dq = σ(2πr dr). Period T = 2π/ω. Current dI = dq/T = σ ω r dr. The magnetic field at the center from this ring is dB = μ₀ dI / 2r = μ₀ σ ω dr / 2. Total field B = ∫(μ₀ σ ω / 2) dr from 0 to R. This evaluates to (μ₀ σ ω R) / 2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charged particle of charge q and mass m is shot with a velocity v into a restricted region of space containing a uniform magnetic field B. The magnetic field region has a strictly finite transverse width d = mv / 2qB. The particle's initial velocity vector is completely perpendicular to the magnetic field lines and also perpendicular to the boundary plane of the region. By what exact angle θ is the particle's velocity vector deflected by the time it exits the magnetic field region?
questions.explanation: The radius of the circular trajectory inside the magnetic field is R = mv/qB. The region's width is given as d = R/2. Because the particle enters perpendicular to the boundary, the center of curvature lies exactly on the boundary line. By basic geometry of the circular arc, the angle θ of deflection satisfies sin(θ) = d/R = (R/2)/R = 1/2. Therefore, θ = arcsin(0.5) = 30°.
